text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has crept up 0.31% today and 7.81% over the past two weeks, riding a wave of crude oil strength driven by renewed Iran-U.S. tensions and reported attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities. Oil prices have climbed to a six-week high, and U.S. refineries are running at near-maximum capacity (98%), which means refiners like Marathon can process more barrels at higher margins when crude is elevated.

The broader tailwind here is tightening global oil supply combined with strong demand signals—gasoline prices hit record highs for Labor Day weekend, suggesting consumers are still buying fuel despite the cost. With refineries already at near-full utilization and storage levels relatively moderate, the company is well-positioned to capture value from the premium crude environment without being constrained by excess inventory.
